No one relies in this on the word of an astrologer that the sun has been eclipsed when its eclipse has not been seen, or that says it was eclipsed by night, or the moon by day, when it is not seen. The prayer for the eclipse of the sun is prayed only by day, and the prayer for the eclipse of the moon only by night, after the eclipse has been seen. The qunut in the eclipse prayer is in every pair of bowings before the bowing, in the second, the fourth, the sixth, the eighth, and the tenth. There is no harm in reciting in each rakah, at each standing, a surah or more, apportioning the recitation across the bowings. If he does this, he recites the Opening of the Book only at the outset with the surah, making the beginning of each standing the opening of a surah, and likewise when he rises from the prostration into the second.

The eclipse prayer is not to be performed until the eclipse has actually been seen and confirmed. One should not rely on someone merely saying that the sun has eclipsed when he has not seen it himself, nor on a claim made at night that the moon has eclipsed by day, nor by day that the sun has eclipsed by night. The solar eclipse prayer is prayed only during the day, and the lunar eclipse prayer only at night, and in both cases only after the eclipse has been seen.

The qunut in this prayer is performed in every second rakah, before the second, fourth, sixth, eighth, and tenth bowings. It is also permitted to recite in every rakah, and more than that, before bowing. When one does so, the Opening of the Book is recited only at the outset of each surah, so that he makes it the first opening of the surah, and likewise when he rises from the prostration in the second rakah of the eclipse prayer.

These two rakahs, with their four prostrations and their five bowings in each rakah, were the form in which the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (ع), led the people in the eclipse prayer. He prayed it at any time, by night or by day, whether traveling or resident in a city. If the eclipse fell at the time of an obligatory prayer, he would begin with the obligatory prayer. But if he had already entered the eclipse prayer and feared that the time of the obligatory prayer would lapse, he would interrupt the eclipse prayer, perform the obligatory prayer, and then, having finished it, resume and build upon what he had already completed of the eclipse prayer. In the same manner he prayed at every sign that occurred, whether wind, darkness, tremors, earthquakes, or any other portent, just as the eclipse prayer is prayed. Whoever misses the eclipse prayer, or the prayer of the signs, does not make it up. It is recommended that the eclipse prayer be performed in an open, cleared space so that the clearing of the eclipse may be seen. If the imam departs, those who can see the eclipse should be informed of it; and if he does not depart, the people are instructed to remain seated in their places, as we have mentioned.

> وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب

As for the prayer of al-Istisqa, the seeking of rain, Allah Almighty said: "And when Moses sought water for his people, We said: Strike the rock with your staff" (Al-Baqarah: 60). It is narrated that when the people of Moses (ع) were in need of water, and rain later fell upon Madinah, the Messenger of Allah went out and prayed for it, and they were so drenched that they grew concerned for themselves from the intensity of the rain. We have narrated from the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that the prayer of al-Istisqa is like the two Eid prayers. The imam goes out, and the people go out to the prayer ground in humility before their Lord, in fear and self-abasement, and they do not carry weapons as they do for the Eid. The imam prays two rakahs without the call to prayer and without the iqamah, giving the takbeer as he gives it for the two festival prayers, and reciting in them as he recites for the two Eids. Then he ascends the pulpit, and when he reaches the top he sits briefly, then stands and turns his cloak, placing what was on his right side onto his left and what was on his left onto his right, as the Messenger of Allah did.

He begins his sermon with the takbeer, the tahleel, and the seeking of forgiveness, offering as much of this as he is able. Then he praises Allah and sends blessings upon the Prophet and his family, and he urges the people to seek forgiveness, to repent, and to do good deeds, making them aware that rain is withheld on account of their sins. He repents to Allah Almighty on their behalf, asks Him, and implores Him for water and mercy to the extent that he is able. It is recommended that this prayer be performed on a Monday.

Concerning the prayers of the Shaf, the Witr, and the two rakahs of Fajr, Allah Almighty said: "By the even and the odd" (Al-Fajr: 3), swearing by all of that. The shaf, in the speech of the Arabs, is the paired or even, and the witr is the odd. In prayer, the witr consists of three rakahs, a sunnah of the night prayer performed after the final Isha, and no prayer is prayed after it until the dawn breaks. The name witr is applied to all three rakahs; it may also refer to the single final rakah, with the two rakahs before it being the shaf, and this is what is preferred in what is established from the words of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ). The worshipper gives the salam after the two rakahs, then stands and prays a single rakah as witr.

There has come strong encouragement toward the witr, which the Messenger of Allah commanded, saying that Allah is witr and loves the witr, so pray the witr, O people of the Quran. Ali (ع) was severe regarding it and did not permit its abandonment. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said that the witr ought not to be abandoned, yet it is not among the prescribed obligatory prayers but is of the sunnah; it is recommended that whoever misses it make it up, though this is not obligatory upon him as a prescribed duty, since it is not among the obligations. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) granted a dispensation that the witr may be prayed while traveling upon a mount, as the supererogatory prayers are prayed. They preferred that the witr be prayed at the end of the night, and whoever prays it at the beginning of the night has fulfilled it.

They preferred that in its two rakahs one recite the Opening of the Book, and in the first of them "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created" (Al-Ala (اَلْأَعْلَى)), and in the second the Opening of the Book and "Say: O disbelievers" (Al-Kafirun), and in the third "Say: He is Allah, the One" (Al-Ikhlas (اَلْإِخْلَاص)) after the Opening of the Book. In the witr he performs the qunut after bowing, raising his hands in it and supplicating with whatever comes readily to him. In the Fajr prayer he performs the qunut before bowing and after the recitation. The two rakahs of Fajr are prayed before the Fajr prayer: the call to Fajr is given, and then he prays two rakahs after the dawn has broken. It is preferred to keep them light, reciting in the first the Opening of the Book and "Say: O disbelievers," and in the second the Opening of the Book and "Say: He is Allah, the One." He then makes the tashahhud, remains seated in his place of prayer, and continues to supplicate until he prays the Fajr. They said (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that there is nothing in supplication that is fixed and appointed such that no other will suffice in its place, neither in the prayer nor outside it; whoever wishes to supplicate may call upon Allah Almighty with whatever he wishes.

We have narrated from the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) many forms of supplication and qunut, all of which show that there is nothing fixed and appointed in it, as we have said. The least and lightest of the qunut is that one glorify Allah within it with three glorifications. There have come from them (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) long, short, and medium supplications for the qunut of the witr and the qunut of the Fajr. Among what has come from them of the medium kind, upon which the narrations agree, is that they instructed that one say in the qunut of the witr:

"O Allah, You see and are not seen, and You are in the highest of vantages. To You are lifted the eyes and moved the feet; toward You necks are stretched and hands spread open; by tongues You are called upon, and to You deeds are submitted. O You to whom hands are stretched out, O You to whom hearts have turned, O You before whom eyes are cast down, O You to whom necks are bowed: we complain to You of the hardship of the age, the massing of enemies, the fewness of our number, and the division of our hearts. We give thanks to You for Your blessings through our guardian and our imam, the son of the daughter of our Prophet, named the imam of his age, our guide to You and the one who points us to You. We ask You to send blessings upon him and upon his forefathers, and to support him with a victory by which You give might to Your religion and by which You aid Your friends. O Allah, gather hearts upon Your obedience and his obedience and upon holding to his imamate, and support him against his renegade enemies, O God of creation, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, make certainty firm in my heart, and increase me in light, guidance, and forgiveness, and guide me to Your straight path. Ameen, Ameen. I ask You, my Lord, for good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and I ask You to guard me from the torment of the Fire."

Whoever wishes to lengthen the supplication may add to it as he wishes. And in the qunut of the Fajr:

"O Allah, we praise You, and seek Your help, and seek Your forgiveness, and extol You with good, and give thanks to You and do not deny You; we humble ourselves to You and submit to You, and we disown whoever is wicked toward You and denies You. O Allah, You alone we worship, and to You we pray and prostrate, and to You we strive and hasten; we hope for Your mercy and fear Your severe punishment, for Your punishment surely overtakes the disbelievers. O Allah, punish the disbelievers, the hypocrites, the liars, and those who deny Your friends, the imams from the pure family of Your Prophet, and send down upon them Your scourge, Your might, Your anger, and Your torment. O Allah, punish the disbelievers among the People of the Book, and the idolaters, men and women. Forgive me, and the believing men and women and the Muslim men and women, and set right what is between them, and unite their word upon Your obedience and the obedience of Your friends, and make firm in their hearts faith and wisdom, and steady them upon the religion of Your Prophet, and support them against Your enemy and their enemy. O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, take me into Your care among those You have taken, heal me among those You have healed, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and none decrees against You. He whom You befriend is not humiliated, and he whom You oppose is not honored. Blessed are You and exalted. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You, and I ask You, my Lord, for good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and I ask You to guard me from the torment of the Fire."

And in the qunut of the Friday prayer and in the qunut of the eclipse:

"There is no god but Allah, the Wise, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the High, the Great. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and all that is within them and between them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and make my heart firm upon Your religion and the religion of Your Prophet, and let not my heart swerve after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from Yourself, for You are the Bestower. O Allah, make me one of those You have created for Your Garden and chosen for Your religion, and turn to me in acceptance, for You are capable of all things, and You are the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful. And send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You are worthy of it and as they are worthy of it from You, may (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ)."

As for the obligatory prayer, it is seventeen rakahs in each day and night. The Dhuhr prayer is the first of them, called the first because it was the first prayer that the Messenger of Allah prayed, at the hour in which the obligation of prayer was sent down upon him. It is four rakahs. In the first two he recites the Opening of the Book and a surah and makes the tashahhud after them, and in the last two he recites the Opening of the Book alone, then makes the tashahhud and the tasleem. The Asr is likewise four rakahs, as Dhuhr, with the same recitation. The Maghrib is three rakahs: he makes the tashahhud after two rakahs, reciting aloud in them, then rises and prays a third rakah in which he recites the Opening of the Book silently, then sits, makes the tashahhud, and departs. The final Isha is four rakahs, like Dhuhr, except that he recites aloud in its first two rakahs. Then the Fajr is two rakahs in which he recites aloud. That is seventeen rakahs.

The sunnah prayer is the like of the obligatory prayer in number, its recitation all silent, though if one wishes he may recite a little aloud in the night prayer. He gives the salam from all of it after every two rakahs, and in each rakah he recites the Opening of the Book and a surah. These are six rakahs before Dhuhr, after the sun has passed its zenith, and four after it; four rakahs before Asr, after which there is no prayer until the sun sets; six rakahs after Maghrib before the final Isha, and four before Isha and four after it; and the witr, three rakahs, from which he gives the salam after two, then rises and prays the third, then prays two rakahs seated; and two rakahs before the Fajr prayer. That is, in number, thirty-five rakahs; but since the two rakahs seated are counted as one rakah of standing, the total is thirty-four, which is the like of the obligatory prayer. It is called the sunnah prayer because the Messenger of Allah used to pray it and bound himself to it, and likewise the imams from his progeny (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) bound themselves to it, commanded their friends and their followers to it, encouraged them toward it, and mentioned to them its merit and its reward.

> وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةًۭ لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًۭا مَّحْمُودًۭا

As for the supererogatory prayer, it has no limit. It is a voluntary act; whoever wishes prays of it what he wishes at the times in which prayer is permitted, by night or by day. It is narrated of Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) that he used to pray a thousand rakahs in each day and night when he was able, and the most excellent of this is what is prayed at night and kept vigil with after sleep. Allah Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad: "And in a part of the night keep vigil with it, as an additional prayer for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station" (Al-Isra: 79). Of a man it is said that he "hajada" when he sleeps, and "tahajjada" when he rises from sleep for some matter he intends; so he awakes from his sleep for it and keeps vigil with it as an additional prayer, meaning with the Quran. And He said: "O you who are wrapped in garments, rise the night except a little, half of it, or lessen from it a little" (Al-Muzzammil: 1-4), to the end of it.

> وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۢ

The Messenger of Allah used to stand at night until his feet would swell from the length of his standing, and he forbade a man to sleep the whole night through, so that he would be like a carcass thrown down. It is recommended to prolong the standing in the night prayer, and one ought not to abandon it, but rather to set for himself a fixed portion of it. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: I hold in contempt the servant who has read the Quran and then wakes in the night yet does not rise, until, when the morning draws near, he rises and hurries through his prayer. Whoever has not read the whole of the Quran may recite of it what comes readily to him. Allah Almighty said: "So recite what is easy for you of the Quran" (Al-Muzzammil: 20). Whoever wishes may stand the whole night with a single surah that he repeats, or with part of it, or with two surahs, or with more than that. There is no harm in reciting, in the supererogatory prayer, part of a surah in the rakah together with the Opening of the Book, or in joining two surahs within it, or many surahs. Some of them would stand the whole night, or most of it, with a single verse that he repeated whenever he came to it, a verse of promise and warning, pondering it and repeating it so that he might understand it and grow humble before it. They preferred to open the night prayer with two light rakahs and then to pray after them whatever one wishes.

> مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ

The most excellent form of the supererogatory prayer, of charity, and of all the works of righteousness is what is done in concealment and in secret; and the most excellent way to render the whole of the obligatory acts, the prayer, the zakat, and others, is openly. All the supererogatory prayers are not to be prayed in congregation, neither in the month of Ramadan nor in any other, and the people are to pray them only singly. The most excellent place for them is the houses, for in their concealment and secrecy lies their merit. The Messenger of Allah once prayed a voluntary prayer at night in the mosque during the month of Ramadan, and the people ranged themselves behind him, praying with his prayer, so he forbade them from that, entered his chamber, and prayed within it. The first to make the standing in congregation during Ramadan a practice was Umar ibn al-Khattab; yet had there been merit in it, the Messenger of Allah would not have forbidden it, and he would have been the foremost to reach it before Umar and others. The common people have narrated this very account from the Messenger of Allah, and then followed Umar in it, in opposition to the Prophet and in defiance of his prohibition. And Allah Almighty says: "Let those who go against his command beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them" (Al-Nur: 63), and He says: "Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it, and fear Allah" (Al-Hashr: 7). The most they have said in this matter is that the Messenger of Allah disliked it and forbade it only for those who did it with him, lest it become an obligation upon the people.

You do not claim that he granted a license to others in this matter, for had there been a license in it he would have spoken of it as a prophet, may Allah bless him and his family. When he forbade a thing, it was because Allah Almighty had made the ruling plain, and Allah had made the clear declaration an obligation upon him. So you are bound to refrain from what he forbade you, just as Allah Almighty commanded, unless a clear allowance reaches you for what you claim is permitted. They claim it was permitted, yet the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, neither did it in the days of his life, nor in the days of Abu Bakr, nor in the early days of Umar. It appeared only in Umar's later period. By their own reckoning this makes it an innovation, and some of them acknowledge this while calling it a good innovation. But this contradicts the word of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family: "Every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance leads to the Fire. Follow, and do not innovate." How can an innovation be good when Allah Almighty forbade it upon the tongue of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family?

In the same way they invented the Duha prayer, which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, had forbidden. A man of the Ansar asked Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) about it, and he answered him: "Were your own people, the Ansar, not the first to invent it?" The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, had forbidden it. They used to come from their homes and enter the mosque in the forenoon and pray, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade them from that. Then Yazid ibn Muawiyah revived it at the severed head of al-Husayn (ع) in the forenoon: he rose and prayed two rakahs and made it a fixed practice for himself, not out of anything his people held against him for what he had committed, but taking it, by his own claim, as a thanksgiving for what he had done, though it will only sink him deeper in the blaze of Hell.

Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) held that a person should make up whatever voluntary prayers he had missed when he was kept occupied from them or overtaken by sleep. This is not an obligation, but he loved, may Allah's blessings be upon him, not to cut off or let go to waste anything that Allah Almighty had made a part of his devotion. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Whoever intends to rise in the night, and takes to his bed, let him say: O Allah, do not leave me safe from Your cunning, and do not make me forget Your remembrance, and do not place me among the heedless. I will rise, Allah willing, at such and such an hour. Then Allah Almighty appoints for him an angel, an angel of that hour, who rouses him." And he said: "Whoever intends something of the night vigil, and sleep overcomes his eyes until morning, his sleep is a charity to him from Allah, and Allah owes him the reward of his intention and completes for him the vigil of his night."

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Allah has an angel who, when half the night has passed, declares: Glorified and Holy is our Lord, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit, our Lord the Merciful, there is no god but He. Let those who strive arise. So whoever Allah wills arises. Then he falls silent as long as Allah wills, then he says: Glorified and Holy is our Lord, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit, our Lord the Merciful, there is no god but He. Let those who remember arise. So whoever Allah wills arises. Then when dawn breaks he says: Glorified and Holy is our Lord, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit, our Lord the Merciful, there is no god but He. Let the heedless arise."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said that when a third of the night has passed a caller cries out: "O seeker of good, draw near. O seeker of evil, hold back. Is there one who repents, that he may be turned to in mercy? Is there one who seeks forgiveness, that he may be forgiven? Is there one who asks, that his request may be granted? O Allah, grant every one who spends a replacement, and grant every one who withholds ruin." This call goes out every night from the passing of a third of the night until morning, and on the night of Friday from the first of the night to its last. He said: when a third of the night remains, the gates of heaven are opened, and the angel calls out in this way until morning.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "The people of the highest ranks are set level in the Garden upon dappled horses whose bridles are of gold and whose saddles are of pearl and ruby. They pass by those who are below them, who say: Our Lord, by what have You brought Your servants to this honor? And it is said to them: They used to rise in the night while you slept, and they used to fast in the day while you ate, and they used to fight while you shrank in cowardice, and they used to spend in the way of Allah while you were miserly."

As for the mention of prostration in the Quran, Allah Almighty said: ﴿ وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ ﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 21], meaning at the places of prostration within it. We have narrated from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that there are fifteen prostrations in the Quran. Whoever recites them, or hears them recited, should prostrate. Some of them are obligatory, such that one is not permitted to omit the prostration at that point, and we will note these as they come.

The first prostration of the Quran is at the end of Surah al-Araf. Then in Surah al-Ra'd, at "and their shadows in the mornings and evenings." In Surah al-Nahl, at "and they do what they are commanded." In Surah al-Isra, at "and it increases them in reverence." In Surah Maryam, at "they fell down prostrate and weeping." In Surah al-Hajj, at "Allah does what He wills," and in it also at "and do good, that you may succeed." In Surah al-Furqan, at "and it increases their aversion." In Surah al-Naml, at "the Lord of the mighty Throne." In Surah al-Sajdah, at "and they are not arrogant," and this is one of the obligatory ones. In Surah Sad, at "and he bowed low and turned in repentance." In Surah Fussilat, at "if it is He whom you worship," and this is one of the obligatory ones. And at the end of Surah al-Najm, which is likewise obligatory. In Surah al-Inshiqaq, at "and when the Quran is recited to them, they do not prostrate." And at the end of Surah al-Alaq, at "Read in the name of your Lord who created," and this too is one of the obligatory ones.

Whoever is in prayer and hears a reciter reciting a verse of prostration, or has it recited before him, and does not prostrate for it, should incline his head in a nod, or he may form the intention of prostration if it is one of the obligatory ones. They disliked reciting in an obligatory prayer a surah containing one of the obligatory prostrations, for if he recites it he must prostrate, even should the verse fall at the end of the surah. In that case he prostrates, then rises and recites the Opening of the Book, then bows and prostrates. In what lies outside the obligatory prostrations he has the choice: if he wishes he prostrates, and if he wishes he does not. Whoever recites a verse of prostration while riding prostrates in whatever direction he faces, nodding with his head. There is no takbir in the prostration of the Quran, and no tashahhud, and no taslim. It is to be performed by whoever hears it, whether he was attentively listening to the Quran or reciting it himself, even if he is not in a state of ablution. He glorifies Allah while prostrate, and asks of Allah Almighty and calls upon Him with whatever he wishes.

The chapters of zakat open here, and with them the command to give it, the encouragement toward it, and the severity that attends its withholding. Allah the Almighty said: "Successful indeed is he who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, and prays" [al-Ala]. And He said: "Blessed be the believers who are humble in their prayers, and who turn away from ill speech, and who are active in giving zakat" [al-Muminun]. And He said: "Establish the prayer and pay the zakat." The Almighty said: "When the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and take them, and confine them, and wait for them at every lookout. But if they repent, establish prayer, and pay zakat, then let them go their way" [al-Tawbah: 5]. So Allah does not accept the Islam of a polytheist who withholds zakat, and He said: "Woe to the polytheists who do not pay zakat" [al-Fussilat: 6-7].

The Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) was asked about this verse, "Woe to the polytheists who do not pay zakat," and he said: Allah does not reproach the polytheists for it. Have you not heard His words, "Woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayers, who make a show of themselves and withhold the maun"? For the maun is zakat. Then he said: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none betrays Allah in anything of the zakat of his wealth except a polytheist.

And he (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) said: When Allah wills good for a servant, He sends an angel from among the keepers of Paradise, who wipes his breast so that his soul grows generous with zakat. And he said: Whoever gives the zakat of his wealth, let him give it with a willing soul, for he gives only a portion of what Allah has given him, and Allah stores away the rest for him; and whoever gives the zakat of his wealth, its evil has departed from him. And he said: No wealth is ever destroyed on land or sea except through the withholding of zakat from it; so fortify your wealth with zakat, treat your sick with charity, and turn away affliction with supplication. And he said: No one gives the zakat of his wealth and finds his wealth thereby diminished, nor withholds it and finds it thereby increased, nor does any wealth decrease through charity; so give, and do not shrink from it. And he said: Allah the Almighty has tracts of ground that are called the parched wastes, to which is driven whoever withholds Allah's due from his wealth, so that he is left in want among them.

And he (ع) said: Whoever has camels or cattle or sheep and does not pay their zakat will be laid out flat on the Day of Resurrection upon a barren, level plain, and they will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns and bite him with their mouths; whenever the last of them has passed over him, the first of them returns to him, until the reckoning of all creation is finished.

From the Commander of the Believers, Ali (ع), it is related that he said: The worshipper has three signs: prayer, zakat, and fasting. And the Prophet (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) said in his bequest to al-Hasan (ع): I counsel you, O Hasan, and all my children and the people of my house, and whoever among the believers this writing of mine reaches, to fear Allah your Lord. And Allah, Allah, regarding zakat, for it extinguishes the anger of Allah from you.

And he (ع) said: Allah the Almighty has made obligatory upon the wealthy, from their wealth, the measure that suffices their poor. If the poor go hungry or naked, it is because of what the wealthy withhold, and Allah the Almighty will hold them to account for that on the Day of Resurrection and punish them severely. And he said: Whoever amasses wealth and does not pay its due, his wealth becomes a serpent that will devour him on the Day of Resurrection. And he said: The withholder of zakat is like the devourer of riba, and no one who withholds zakat is a Muslim.

And he (ع) said concerning the words of Allah the Almighty, "They will be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection" [Al Imran: 180]: The wealth on which zakat was withheld is fashioned into the likeness of a bald serpent that winds about his neck and bites at him until the people are finished with the reckoning, and it says: I am your wealth, whose zakat you withheld. And he said concerning the words of Allah the Almighty, "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, give them tidings of a painful punishment, on the day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and with it will be branded their foreheads, their sides, and their backs. This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard" [al-Tawbah: 34-35]: The hoard is the wealth on which zakat is not paid; but wealth whose zakat has been paid is no hoard. As the Prophet (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) said: On the Day of Resurrection there will be brought the wealth of one who withheld its zakat, and it will be beaten into plates, then heated in the fire of Hell, and with them his forehead, his sides, and his back will be branded; whenever they cool, they are heated again and the branding resumed, until the reckoning of all creation is finished. And he said: Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth has discharged what was owed upon him in it.

A man asked Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) about a man who complained to him that he was seized with terror in his sleep, as though a woman were pressing a demand upon him and frightening him. He said: This is a man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth. The questioner reported this to the man, who said: By Allah, I do pay it. The questioner conveyed that back to Abu Abd Allah (ع), and he said: If that is so, then he does not place it in its proper place. The man said: As for that, yes.

**The payment of zakat to its rightful recipients, and the prohibition of placing it elsewhere.**

> خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَلِهِمْ صَدَقَةًۭ تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا

Allah the Almighty said to Muhammad, His Prophet (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ): "Take from their wealth a charity that will purify them and cleanse them by it" [al-Tawbah: 103]. Then He informed him of the places in which it is to be set, and said: "Charity is only for the poor and the destitute, and those who administer it, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for freeing captives, and for those in debt, and in the cause of Allah, and for the wayfarer, an obligation from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise" [al-Tawbah: 60].

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: The poor is the needy man who does not beg from people; the destitute is one in even greater hardship, the one who begs from people. Those who administer it are the collectors of the charity who take charge of receiving it from the people. Those whose hearts are to be reconciled are men of enmity who nonetheless hold power and standing and obedience among their people; such a one is given from the zakat so that he may be won over and may incline toward obedience those who follow him, as the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ) used to give to the chiefs of the tribes in order to reconcile them, men such as Uyayna ibn Husn and al-Aqra ibn Habis. Their like exists in every age, and whenever they exist the imams give to them from the zakat. "In the freeing of captives" is manumission; "those in debt" are the people burdened with debts; "in the cause of Allah" is in the struggle; and "the wayfarer" is the stranger cut off from his means.

These, then, are eight categories upon whom Allah the Almighty has made the charities obligatory. It is not proper that one category be given the whole of it to the exclusion of another, for there is no dispute among the Muslims on this. Consider: if a man were to name several men by name and set a sum for them, and one of them rose up to claim the whole of it for himself without handing his companions their share, this would not be lawful for him. How much less lawful, then, for one who has heard the words of Allah the Almighty, "Charity is only for the poor and the destitute, and those who administer it," until He has named all eight categories, and who then gives it to a single category among them, when he is bound with this to hand it over to the one whom Allah has commanded to receive it. Allah has made it an obligation upon that one to set it in its proper places, has entrusted to him the oversight of it and the knowledge of the state of each class of its people, and of the measure that should be given at every time and season according to what befalls the Muslims and Islam. This is what none can know or fulfill except the Imams, whom Allah the Almighty has charged with the affairs of His servants and set over His earth and His lands.

The people do not differ that the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) himself took charge of receiving the charities from those present with him, and sent his agents to receive them from those distant, who then brought them to him so that he might distribute them where Allah commanded them distributed. Allah made this clear and plain in mentioning those who administer the charity in His Book and assigning them a share of it for their labor upon it, just as He said to His Messenger (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ), "Take from their wealth a charity" [al-Tawbah: 103]. When He then took him to Himself, the people did not differ that this obligation remained, undiminished by the passing of the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ); rather they agreed that whoever stands in his place takes charge of receiving it as he received it (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) and directs it to the mentioned channels. They agreed with Abu Bakr upon fighting those who withheld the zakat, named them the people of apostasy, and held their blood lawful. Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and the Commander of the Believers Ali (ع) each took charge of receiving it in their days, none differing with them or disputing it.

When the affair passed to the Banu Umayya and the people saw that they had cut it off for themselves, some held back from paying the zakat to them and turned in alarm to those who remained of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) and questioned them about it. Every one of them commanded that it be paid to the rulers, and said: upon them is what they have taken on, and upon you is what you have taken on; you are to give it to them, and it is upon them to set it in its proper places. Thus they related from Aisha, Abu Hurayra, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Said al-Khudri, and Abd Allah ibn Umar, and they related no contrary word from any of the Companions, nor do they relate any disagreement among them. When Ibn Umar was pressed with much questioning, he said: Woe to you. Tell me: if I were to seize thieves and cut off the hands of some of them and leave the rest, would you be in the right? They said no. He said: And if you handed them to the ruler and he did that, would it be upon you? They said no. He said: So too do these matters run. Pay it to them, even if with it they devour the flesh of serpents.

This is the word of the generality and what they relate from their predecessors, though today the whole of them has stripped it away and departed from it altogether, without a proof they have advanced or a cause they have brought. Rather they have entered into the company of those whom they themselves reckoned people of apostasy for withholding from their rulers the zakat of their wealth, just as those others withheld their zakat from Abu Bakr. And for that withholding there is a ground which this is not the place to mention, whose exposition would grow long were it set down.

As for the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), they do not hold that zakat is to be paid to any but the Imams of guidance from the household of the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ), whom Allah the Almighty has commanded His servants to obey in His Book and whom He has entrusted with the affairs of His servants. Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth willingly to other than them, it does not suffice for him, and he must pay it to the Imam of his age from among them. But if the imams of injustice overpower him and take it from him by force, that suffices for him. The Commander of the Believers Ali (ع) said to one of his agents over al-Jazira: Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth to Muawiya and his agents, of those whom our cavalry and our men have kept at bay, do not credit that to him, but take it from him, for it did not reach him and did not protect him. But where they overpowered a man and took it from him by force, accept his word and do not press him.

And he (ع) said: The Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) forbade a man to conceal his zakat from his imam, and said that this is hypocrisy. Allah the Almighty has made clear to His servants, upon the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ), to whom they are to hand their charities, in that He appointed them trustees over it, since He forbade it to them and to none besides. The community is agreed that it is not lawful for the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) nor for the people of his house. They related that al-Hasan ibn Ali (ع), while a small boy, took a date from the dates of the charity and put it into his mouth, and the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) looked at him and hastened to him and drew it out of his mouth with its moisture upon it and threw it back among the dates of the charity, and said: We, the people of the house, charity is not lawful for us. So He informed them that they are the trusted ones over it, charged with receiving it and setting it in its proper places, and that this belongs to none besides them, to no one else at all among the people.

In like manner He assigned to them the fifth (اَلْخُمْس) which He assigned to the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ), as a token of their trustworthiness and their standing in the place of the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) after him in that for his community. This belongs to the Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) among them, and not to the rest, for the rest of them are bound in what is due from them, like the rest of the community, to pay their charities to the Imam, just as the rest of the people are bound, as was the state of the household of the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) with him in his lifetime. It is for one after another, an honor passed on and a virtue kept unbroken. Whoever has denied their right and been ignorant of their trustworthiness, the least that binds him by the word of the Imams and his own predecessors, when Allah makes their affair manifest and gives them dominion over the one who denied them, is that he pay them the zakat of his wealth in every one of his states. We have already set down what suffices of the proof in this, though we have made it brief, for whoever is granted its understanding, and Allah guides to his right course.

**The zakat of gold, silver, and precious substances.**

We have narrated from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that zakat is not due on gold until it reaches twenty mithqals, with a full year having turned over it in the possession of the one who came by it; nor on silver until it reaches two hundred dirhams, with a full year having turned over it in the possession of the one who came by it. When the year has turned over it in the possession of its owner, then upon the twenty mithqals is half a mithqal, and upon the two hundred dirhams is five dirhams; and this has become a nisab in his hand. Whatever exceeds it bears a quarter of a tenth, if he came by it before the head of the year, due at the head of the year, and he pays it out likewise. If at the head of the year it falls short of this measure, there is no zakat upon it; and whatever exceeds bears zakat by that reckoning. The one is not joined to the other, and no zakat is due on gold or on silver until each of the two reaches the measure we have mentioned.

If a man has one hundred dirhams and ten dinars whose value is one hundred dirhams or more, there is no zakat upon him in that, until the dinars reach twenty dinars and the dirhams reach two hundred dirhams and the year has turned over it, unless he spends some of it before the year in flight from the zakat. If he does that, zakat is upon him. This is like a man who had two hundred dirhams and, when he saw that the zakat was becoming due upon him, spent some of it away.

Whoever converts some of his silver into dinars in order to escape the zakat owed on it, or spends some of his dinars for the same purpose, has done what is not permitted. As for mineral wealth such as pearls and amber, when they are drawn out from their source and their place, the fifth is due upon the one who extracts them, and no zakat falls upon what he keeps back. Once he sells such a thing and the buyer takes possession of it, it becomes like the rest of the buyer's wealth: he assesses its value and pays zakat upon it at the completion of the year, if it is held for trade. There is no zakat upon jewelry or upon mineral goods that are taken for personal use, unless a person takes them as a stratagem to flee from zakat. If that is his intent, the intent invalidates the stratagem and zakat is due. The same rule governs what is drawn from the mines, whether gold, silver, brass, iron, lead, mineral stone, or the like: the fifth is due upon it, and once it passes into circulation it is treated like the rest of one's wealth. Whoever holds debased coinage pays its zakat from it in proportion to the pure metal it contains, giving debased for debased; and if it is copper, iron, lead, or some other base metal with a coating over it, its value is referred back to what it truly is in its origin, joined to the rest of his holdings, and zakat is paid upon the whole.

There is no zakat upon clothing, riding animals, household vessels, or furnishings, so long as they are not held for trade and were not acquired as a means of fleeing from zakat. If they are held for trade, or if they were bought with wealth on which zakat was due and then set aside precisely so that no zakat would be paid, then zakat is due upon them. Whoever buys trade goods assesses their value at the head of the year and pays their zakat, provided the goods are present with him or in a place from which he is not barred. So too with a debt owed to him, if he is not prevented from it: when the year turns upon it, its zakat is due, and it is treated as though it were already in his hands. But if he can reach it only through litigation, and the one who owes it refuses him, he does not pay its zakat until he receives it and it comes into his hand. There is no zakat upon the wealth of a child until he reaches maturity, takes possession of it, and a full year passes upon it in his keeping. Yet if that wealth passes into the hand of an adult who trades with it, zakat is due upon it, and the zakat falls upon the one who trades with it; any loss belongs to him, while the profit belongs to the child. The wealth of a woman's dowry follows the rule of a debt, as we have already explained. Whoever pays out the zakat of his wealth to deliver it, and it is lost before it reaches its due place, must make it good again, for he remains its guarantor until he sets it where it belongs. And whoever dies still owing zakat he did not discharge, it is taken from the principal of his estate, whether or not he left a bequest to that effect, once it is known and established.

As for the zakat of camels, cattle, and sheep, we have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that there is no zakat upon working camels, those upon which loads are carried or by which irrigation is drawn, whatever their number and however great it grows. But if they are grazing camels, kept at pasture for their increase and their milk, then no zakat is due upon fewer than five. When they reach five and a year has passed upon them, one sheep is due; there is nothing more upon what exceeds five until they reach ten, when two sheep are due; at fifteen, three sheep; at twenty, four sheep. At twenty-five a bint makhad is due, which is a she-camel that has completed a year since her birth and entered the second, her mother having conceived again after her and being now in labor, not yet delivered. If no bint makhad is found, then an ibn labun suffices, which is a male that has completed two years and entered the third, whose mother conceived after him and gave birth, so that she is now giving milk; and this holds up to thirty-five. When one more is added, a bint labun is due, up to forty-five. If one more is added, a hiqqah is due, which is a she-camel that has completed three years, entered the fourth, and become fit to bear and to be covered; and this holds up to sixty. If one more is added, a jadhaa is due, which is a she-camel that has completed four years and entered the fifth; and this holds up to seventy-five. If one more is added, two daughters of labun are due, up to ninety. If one more is added, two hiqqas are due, up to a hundred and twenty. Beyond that, for every forty a bint labun is due, and for every fifty a hiqqah. If the assessor does not find among the camels the exact age that is owed, he takes the age below it together with two sheep or twenty dirhams, or the age above it and returns two sheep or twenty dirhams.

There is no zakat upon working cattle, those by which one plows and draws water, nor upon the grazing cattle kept for increase and milk until they reach thirty. When they reach thirty and a year has passed upon them in the ownership of their owner, a tabi or tabia is due, which is the yearling whose horns have grown even. There is nothing upon what exceeds thirty until forty, when a musinnah is due. From forty to sixty it is one musinnah; at sixty, two tabi's; at seventy, one musinnah and one tabi; at eighty, two musinnahs; at ninety, three tabi's; at a hundred, one musinnah and two tabi's; and so onward, for every thirty a tabi and for every forty a musinnah, with nothing due for what lies between.

There is no zakat upon the domestic sheep, which are those raised within the houses and not sent to pasture, but upon the grazing flock zakat is due once it reaches forty and a year has passed upon it in its owner's keeping. When it reaches forty, one sheep is taken from its owner, and there is nothing upon what exceeds forty until it reaches a hundred and twenty. If it passes that by one or more, two sheep are due, until it reaches two hundred. If it passes two hundred by one or more, three sheep are due; and when the flock grows large, for every hundred a sheep is due.

Concerning what the workers of charity are to do in the districts they oversee and what they are to take, and concerning the wealth of those whose holdings are mingled, we have narrated from the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), that he appointed Mikhnaf ibn Sulaym al-Azdi over the zakat of Bakr ibn Wail and wrote him a covenant. In it he said: This is what Ibn Abi Talib charged upon Mikhnaf ibn Sulaym when he sent him to gather the charity. He commanded him to fear Allah his Lord in all his affairs and in the hidden acts of his conduct, where there is no witness over him but Allah and no watchful guardian besides Him. He commanded him not to let his obedience to Allah in what appears outwardly differ from what he keeps concealed, for whoever does that has fallen into treachery, has made light of the right of Allah, and has exposed himself to His displeasure. He commanded him to conduct himself with justice among those over whom he is set, to deal fairly with them in what is apportioned, to meet them with an open face and a gentle side, to secure for the wronged among them redress from the one who wronged him, and to hold the balance even among them in his seat, his countenance, his bearing, and his leave to approach, so that no man among them might see any favoring of another over himself. He commanded him not to revile them, nor to scowl upon them, nor to turn from them out of a sense of superiority through the authority he held over them, for they are brothers in religion and helpers against the enemy and aids in the drawing out of what is owed. And he said (ع): You have in this charity, O Mikhnaf ibn Sulaym, a portion and an appointed right, and you have partners in it: the poor, the needy, and the weak of household. If they render you your right, then render them theirs; and if you do not, you will be among the people most beset by adversaries and misery on the Day of Judgment. Woe to the man whose adversary is the poor, the destitute, the ruined, and the wayfarer.

It is narrated from him (ع) that the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) forbade that people be made to swear over their charity, and said of them that they are trusted, meaning trusted as to what is hidden and concealed of their livestock; but what is manifest is taken from them. He said: the one who transgresses in charity is like the one who withholds it, and he forbade that people be dealt with harshly in the matter of charity. The Commander of the Believers, Ali (ع), said: the charity of the people of the open country is taken in their own places, and they are not driven from place to place; and in the year of drought they are granted delay until the land grows green again. It is narrated from him (ع) that the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) forbade the joining of what is separate and the separating of what is joined for the sake of charity. The separating of what is joined is that a man has a hundred and twenty sheep, upon which only a single sheep is due until the number increases; the assessor is forbidden to break them into groups of forty and take three sheep from them. Likewise, if a man owns forty, he is not to be required to divide them into two twenties so as to give no zakat upon them. As for the joining of what is separate, it is that three men, each owning forty sheep and not partners in them, should not be combined so that the assessor takes a single sheep, when, held apart, three sheep would be due. So too the assessor is not to combine the flocks of two men upon each of whom, separately, no zakat is due, so that by joining them zakat becomes due. Nor are partners in livestock charged zakat until each of them holds what makes zakat due upon him; when that is so and their shares are equal, it is taken from them accordingly, and if one holds more than another, they settle the difference between themselves by mutual adjustment. This is like two men who share a flock upon which nothing is due until it reaches eighty; when it reaches eighty, two sheep are due, one upon each of them, if the flock is divided between them in halves. But if one owns a third and the other two-thirds, only a single sheep is due, falling upon the owner of the two-thirds, until the flock reaches a hundred and twenty. If one more is added, two sheep are due, and the two partners settle the difference between them, for the assessor took from the whole flock two sheep, while one owned forty and the other eighty. Thus he took from the owner of two-thirds one sheep and a third, though only one sheep was truly owed by him, and from the owner of forty a third of a sheep, though a full sheep was owed by him; so it comes to rest at one sheep upon each, the shortfall in each one's share being made good against what the assessor took from him.

Upon this same footing runs the rule of all wealth, whether coin, camels, cattle, sheep, grain, or anything upon which zakat is due: when it is held among partners, each partner owes upon his share only what he would have owed were he no partner at all, because partnership does not dissolve ownership nor transfer any part of it from one to another. Each partner has only what he owns; whatever was due upon him before the partnership is what remains due upon him after it. And when men of wealth gather their properties and mingle them without a true partnership between them, from each is taken what is due upon him, and no regard is given to the mingling of their holdings.

Whoever holds a quorum of wealth on which zakat has become due, and a year passes upon it, and he pays what is owed, and then some addition comes to it, joins that addition to it at the head of the second year and pays zakat upon the whole together. Of coin he gives out a quarter of a tenth; of livestock, the increase is reckoned within the count of the herd. If a mother gives birth while the assessor is present over the flock, he does not reckon the newborn, nor take it, nor take its like in charity. He takes from camels and cattle only the ages that have been described, and from sheep only the full-grown; he does not take the aged, nor the defective, nor the male of the flock, nor its choicest, nor its poorest, but takes from the middling. If the assessor and the owners of the wealth fall into dispute, the owners choose a third of the flock and set it apart, and the assessor chooses from the remaining two-thirds what is due and takes it.

As for the zakat of grains and fruits, Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِى أَنشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَّعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ مُخْتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهًا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ كُلُوا مِن ثَمَرِهِ إِذَا أَثْمَرَ وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾ [Al-Anam: 141]. It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾ [Al-Anam: 141], that he said: this is over and above the obligatory charity; it is given at the time of harvest to the one who asks, who is given the handful, that is, the fistful, and the thing given in charity alongside the imposed obligation. It is narrated from him, from his forefathers, that the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) made it clear beyond all clarity that the tenth is due upon all that the sky and the rivers water, and half the tenth upon what is watered by wells. It has come from the household (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that the tenth is due upon all grains once they have set and ripened; at that point they are appraised, when they first appear, and their owners are given a just estimate. They are then left free to their crop and are held to a tenth of what was estimated. The one who makes the estimate is charged not to press it to the utmost, but to leave something aside. They said: the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) sent Abdullah ibn Rawaha al-Ansari to the people of Khaybar, having been his agent among them upon the half, when the fruit began to ripen. He estimated it upon them, and they objected. So Abdullah ibn Rawaha al-Ansari said to them: I have made my estimate and have not laid more upon you than is right. If you wish, render to us half of what we have estimated; and if you wish, hand it over to us and take half of it. The Jews said: This is the truth by which the heavens and the earth stand. As for honey, they said (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ): if it is held for trade, zakat is due upon it; but what is bought of it, and what is drawn from the combs and cut from the hives, carries no zakat.

As for the zakat of the breaking of the fast, Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى﴾ [Al-Ala]. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said of His words, "He has prospered who purifies himself," that it means he who gives the zakat of the breaking of the fast; and of "and mentions the name of his Lord and prays," that it means the prayer of the festival. He said (ع) that the zakat of the breaking of the fast is a duty upon the rich and the poor alike. The Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) said that the charity of the breaking of the fast is due upon every soul, for himself and for all his dependents, young and old, free and enslaved, a sa of food from each one of them. It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) that he said: a man pays the zakat of the breaking of the fast on behalf of his Jewish and Christian slave. It is narrated from him (ع) that he said: if the slaves of a man's wife are among his dependents, he pays on their behalf; and if they are not among his dependents, then the wife must pay on their behalf. And he (ع) used to pay the zakat of the breaking of the fast on behalf of his father after his father's death, and this is a voluntary good, not an obligation. He said (ع) that one who cannot find food gives in its place dirhams to the value current at the time, and that it is the way of the sunnah to pay the zakat of the breaking of the fast before the festival prayer.

The zakat upon honey follows the same principle that governs merchandise. If the honey is held for trade, then zakat is due upon it. But what a man buys for himself, or draws from his own hives, or cuts from the combs, carries no zakat.

There remains the zakat of the breaking of the fast, the zakat al-fitr. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ﴾. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) explained this verse. His words "He has indeed succeeded who purifies himself" mean the one who pays the zakat al-fitr, and "and remembers the name of his Lord and prays" means the prayer of the Eid.

He (ع) said that the zakat al-fitr is obligatory upon the rich and the poor alike. And the Messenger of Allah (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ) said that the sadaqat al-fitr is due upon every person, on behalf of himself and on behalf of all his dependents, the young among them and the old, the free and the slave. For each one of them the measure is a sa of food.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is related that he said a man pays the zakat al-fitr on behalf of his slave, whether that slave be a Jew or a Christian. And from him (ع) it is related that he said, when a man's wife has slaves who are counted among his dependents, he pays on their behalf; but if they are not among his dependents, then it falls upon the wife to pay on their behalf.

He (ع) used to pay the zakat al-fitr on behalf of his father after his father's death. This is a voluntary act of goodness, not an obligation.

He (ع) said that whoever does not find food should give in its place dirhams according to the value at the time. And the sunnah is that the zakat al-fitr be paid before the fast is broken, before the Eid.

> وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًۭا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍۢ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍۢ

There remains the greatest of the journeys undertaken for the sake of Allah, the Hajj, and what is stated concerning it. Allah Almighty said: "And proclaim the Hajj among the people; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant mountain pass" [al-Hajj: 27]. It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع), from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: When Allah Almighty commanded Ibrahim (ع) to call the people to Hajj, he ascended Mount Safa, placed his finger in his ear, and called out as Allah Almighty had commanded him. His call was heard by those in the east and in the west, even those yet unborn in the loins of their fathers, and they answered him. Whoever fulfills the Hajj once has answered once, whoever fulfills it twice has answered twice, and whoever fulfills it more times has answered accordingly. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: "From this the Talbiyah was made."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hajj is the jihad of every weak person." He also said: "Whoever circumambulates this House seven times and prays two rakahs, the best of prayers, will be forgiven." When he stood on the eve of Arafah, he faced the people and said three times: "Welcome to the delegation of Allah!" Then he said: "Those who ask shall be given, and those who fall short in this world shall be compensated; for every thousand dirhams spent, good deeds are written for them. O people, shall I not give you glad tidings? This evening Allah Almighty commanded His angels, and they descended to the earth, and He said to them: O My angels, look upon My servants, dusty and disheveled, who have come to Me from the ends of the earth. Do you know what they ask? They will say: Our Lord, You know best. And He will say: They ask Me for forgiveness, and I bear witness to you that I have forgiven them."

Hajj carries the reward of the Garden, and Umrah is expiation for every sin. He (ع) said: "Alternate between Hajj and Umrah, for they negate poverty and sins and bring sustenance." He said: "There are sins that cannot be forgiven except at Arafat." Concerning the Hajj caravan he said: "Do not turn them away," meaning that their reward is written for them whether or not you conceal it; no veil is lifted from them unless their evil deeds are removed; and when they have fulfilled their rites it is said to them: "You have built a foundation, so do not demolish it. What has passed is enough for you, so do well in what is to come." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever desires this world and the next, let him come to this House, for whatever a servant has asked of his Lord, Allah will grant him some of it or store it for him." Then he said: "O people, you must perform Hajj and Umrah and alternate between them, for they wash away sins as water washes away grime, and they negate poverty as fire removes the dross of iron."

Ali (ع) used to say that the righteous man, once he has completed the Hajj, takes up his works anew, meaning that he has already been forgiven for what preceded. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) traced back to the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Pilgrims are of three kinds, and the best of them in portion is the man who has been forgiven for his past and future sins. Next is the man who has been forgiven for his past sins and begins his works afresh. Next, and the least of them, is the man who has merely safeguarded his family and his wealth." The pilgrim must inevitably sustain some loss in his wealth, whether through the exertion itself or through a shortfall in his provisioning. Whoever suffers loss in either his wealth or his family while on Hajj has forfeited one of the two rewards, yet he is forgiven for what he has done and what he has deferred, his former sins are forgiven, and he is summoned to fear Allah in what lies ahead.

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: When Allah Almighty sent Adam (ع) down to the earth, he wandered to the House just as he had seen the angels circling the Throne, and he called out to his Lord asking for forgiveness. The call came: "Allah has forgiven you." He said: "O Lord, and my descendants?" And the call came: "O Adam, whoever among your descendants comes to this place bearing his sin as you have borne yours, Allah will forgive him." Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: "The guarantee of the believing pilgrim rests with Allah Almighty, that even if he sins after returning to his family, he remains under Allah's protection for seventy nights." He (ع) said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "Purify My House for those who circumambulate it, those who remain in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate" [al-Baqarah: 125]: "When Allah Almighty revealed that, He sent down upon the Kabah one hundred and seventy mercies: sixty for those who circumambulate it, fifty for those who remain in devotion, forty for those who worship within it, and twenty for those who behold it."

A man asked Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع): "Which is better, voluntary Hajj or voluntary charity?" The questioner kept recalling charity and its virtue, and Abu Abdullah (ع) kept answering that Hajj is better, repeating it several times, until he looked toward the mountain of Abu Qubays and said: "Even if you were to give in charity its weight in gold and silver, you would not attain the reward of Hajj." Then he said: "Is there in charity a circumambulation of the House? Is there in charity a standing at Arafah? Is there in charity anything of the rites?" The questioner said no. He said: "Then Hajj is better."

He (ع) said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "That they may witness benefits for them" [al-Hajj: 28], that these are benefits for them in their religion. He said: "When the believing servant sets out from his home as a pilgrim, he takes no step, and his mount carries him no stage, except that a good deed is written for him by it, an evil deed is erased from him by it, and he is raised a degree by it. When he stands at Arafah, though his sins were as the number of the dust of the earth, they are erased from him. When he casts the pebbles, his rank is raised, to be fulfilled for him on the Day of Resurrection. When he shaves his head, not a hair falls from him but Allah makes its place a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. Whatever he spends is written for him. And when he circumambulates the House, he returns as the day his mother bore him," meaning sound and free of sins. Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty: "Whoever hastens his departure in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever delays, there is no sin on him, for the one who fears Allah" [al-Baqarah: 203]. And he (ع) said: "No one stands upon those mountains, whether righteous or wicked, and calls upon Allah except that He answers him. As for the righteous, he is answered in his Hereafter, and as for the other, he is answered in this world."

> حِجُّ ٱلْبَيْتِ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًۭا ۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنِ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ

On the obligation of Hajj, Allah Almighty said: "And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it; and whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds" [Al Imran: 97]. The Prophet ﷺ said: When this verse was revealed, the people asked: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He remained silent. They asked him twice more, and he said: "No; and had I said yes, it would have become obligatory." Then Allah Almighty revealed: "O you who believe, do not ask about things that, if disclosed to you, would distress you" [al-Maidah: 101]. Ali (ع) said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds" [Al Imran: 97]: "This is said of the one who abandons Hajj while he is able to perform it."

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about the words of Allah Almighty, "for whoever is able to find a way to it" [Al Imran: 97]: what is the ability to find a way? He asked the questioner what people say about it, and the man replied that they say it is provisions and a mount. Abu Abdullah (ع) said: "Abu Jafar (ع) was asked about this, and he said: The people would be ruined then. If a man who has nothing but provisions and a mount, with no sustenance for his family besides that, were compelled to set out with it and not leave it for them, they would indeed be ruined." When asked, then, what the ability is, he said: "The ability to make the journey, sufficient provision for it, the presence of what sustains one's dependents, and the security of the road. Has not Allah Almighty made zakat obligatory only upon the one who possesses two hundred dirhams?"

He (ع) was asked about the man who postpones the Hajj, prevented from it only by a trade that occupies him or a debt he owes, and he said: "He has no excuse; it is not fitting for him to postpone the Hajj, and if he dies, he has abandoned one of the laws of Islam." He (ع) said: "Whoever dies without having performed the Hajj of Islam, not prevented by a need that pressed hard upon him, nor by an illness he could not bear the journey with, nor by a ruler who barred him, let him die a Jew or a Christian." He said: "Hajj is obligatory upon a person once in his lifetime." It was said to him: "And whoever abandons it while able, until he dies?" He said: "He is among those of whom Allah Almighty said, And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind." It was said: "Blind?" He said: "Yes, blind to the path of truth and good." He said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If my ummah were to abandon this House and cease to make for it, they would not be granted respite."

He was asked about the child taken on Hajj, and he said: "That does not suffice for him; the Hajj is upon him when he reaches maturity." He was asked about one who performs Hajj while not knowing this matter, then Allah favors him with its knowledge, and he said: "His Hajj suffices him, though it would be more beloved to me that he perform Hajj again. And if he was a Nasib holding to enmity and performed Hajj upon that, then Allah favored him with knowledge, the Hajj is upon him when he is able." He (ع) said of the owned servant who performs Hajj: "It suffices for him so long as he is owned; and if he is freed, the Hajj is upon him when he is able, for there is no obligation of Hajj upon him while he is owned." Likewise the mother of a child whose master takes her on Hajj: it does not suffice for her. A man may not prevent his wife from the obligatory Hajj if she finds a mahram of hers to travel with her, and provision to spend, and the road is secure. He (ع) said: "The divorced woman may perform Hajj during her waiting period if she wishes." If a man is insolvent and another performs Hajj on his behalf, then he becomes able, the Hajj is still upon him.

> وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا۟ رُءُوسَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْهَدْىُ مَحِلَّهُۥ

He (ع) was asked about Umrah and said: "It is obligatory as the Hajj is obligatory," and he recited the words of Allah Almighty: "And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah" [al-Baqarah: 196]. He said: "Their completion is their performance." He said that a man may bring forward whichever of the two he wishes, the Hajj or the Umrah, and whoever wishes may join them together. Whoever joins them and drives the offering does not leave the state of ihram until he has sacrificed, and that is the qarin, because Allah Almighty says: "Do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place." And whoever has no offering with him and joins them is performing tamattu: when he comes to Mecca he performs tawaf and say and leaves ihram, and that is the Umrah; then he enters ihram for the Hajj from Mecca. Allah Almighty said: "Then whoever enjoys Umrah until the Hajj, then whatever offering is feasible." Abu Abdullah (ع) said: "A sheep, or more than that."

As for what one who intends the Hajj should do, Allah Almighty said: "Hajj is during well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, let there be no lewdness nor wickedness nor quarreling in Hajj" [al-Baqarah: 197]. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: The well-known months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qidah, and Dhu al-Hijjah; Hajj is made obligatory in none but these. The making of Hajj obligatory upon oneself is the Talbiyah, the ishar, and the taqlid; whichever of these the one intending Hajj performs, he has made the Hajj obligatory upon himself. Lewdness is intercourse; wickedness is lying, cursing, and quarreling; and quarreling is a man's saying "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah," and boasting.

Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) said to Abu Khalid al-Wasiti, counseling him when he wished to perform Hajj: "O Abu Khalid, when you set out for Mecca, God willing, then hold to the fear of Allah, remember Him abundantly, and speak little except in good, for the completion of Hajj and Umrah lies in a man's guarding his tongue, as Allah Almighty said: No lewdness, no wickedness, no quarreling in Hajj. Lewdness is intercourse; wickedness is lying, cursing, and quarreling; and quarreling is a man's saying No, by Allah and Yes, by Allah, and boasting. Hold to scrupulousness, which restrains you from disobedience to Allah, to forbearance, by which you master your anger, and to good companionship with those who travel with you. There is no power except by Allah."

Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said to a man he was counseling: "When you go out as a pilgrim, hold to the fear of Allah, to forbearance, to scrupulousness, and to good companionship with those who accompany you, for Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: No account is taken of one who makes for this House if he does not possess three qualities: scrupulousness that restrains him from disobedience to Allah, forbearance by which he masters his anger, and good companionship for those who travel with him."

And Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said to a man who wished to perform Hajj, counseling him: "When you depart from your home intending Hajj or Umrah, make the supplication of relief and say: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous; there is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Great; glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Throne; and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, open before me in this journey of mine with good and seal it for me with good, and preserve me from every creature whose forelock You hold, for You, my Lord, are upon a straight path. In the name of Allah I have set out, in the name of Allah I enter, and for the sake of Allah I journey. O Allah, I place before me my forgetfulness and my haste. In the name of Allah and by the will of Allah, whatever of this journey of mine I remember or forget, O Allah, You are the One whose help is sought over all affairs, the Companion in travel and the Successor over family, wealth, and children. O Allah, make our journey easy for us, fold up the earth for us, and let us travel through it in obedience to You and obedience to Your Messenger. O Allah, set right our affairs for us, bless us in what You have provided us, and guard us from the torment of the Fire."

When you set out upon the road, there is a way to place yourself in Allah's keeping from the very first step. When you set your leg among the travelers, say: "In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and Allah is the Greatest." When you are settled in your journey, praise Allah seven times, glorify Him seven times, magnify Him seven times, and say "La ilaha ill Allah" seven times, and say: "Praise be to Allah who guided us to Islam and honored us with Muhammad, (ع) and his family. Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, for we could not have subdued it ourselves, and indeed to our Lord we shall return. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, You are the Carrier upon the back and the Helper in affairs. O Allah, grant us the best of news, and lead us to Your forgiveness and Your pleasure. O Allah, no bird flies but by Your leave, and no good comes but from You, and none else protects. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, from the distress of turning back, and from an ill return to family, wealth, and children. O Allah, I ask You in this journey of mine for piety, for contentment, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, cut short the distance for me and make it easy, and set aright my affairs and leave me well among my family." And when you return, say in your returning: "We are those who repent, who worship, who praise, returning to our Lord, giving thanks, devoted, and to Him we return."

As for entering the city of the Prophet (ص), the Commander of the Believers (ع) said in his sermon that the Messenger of Allah (ص) declared Madinah sacred between the mountains of Ayr and Thawr, and that whoever causes an unlawful act therein or shelters one who commits it has upon him the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people, and Allah will not accept from him any obligatory or supererogatory act. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said that the two sides of Madinah are sanctified. When he was asked what its two sides were, he answered that it is whatever the free woman surrounded with her garment, which is to say what the Messenger of Allah (ص) prohibited: disturbing its inhabitants, hunting its game, and cutting its trees.

It is recommended to perform a ritual bath before entering the city, and to begin the visit at the Mosque of the Prophet (ص). One should stand at his grave, offer prayers upon him and his family, and testify to his prophethood and his message. One should pray whatever one is able, and then pray two rakahs before sitting at the pillar that stands forward on the side of the grave, from the corner of the grave, for that is the place nearest the head of the Prophet (ص). Then one should rise, approach the grave, and say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger; and I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, truly; and I testify that you are Muhammad ibn Abd Allah; and I testify that you conveyed the message of your Lord and gave sincere counsel to your nation, and that you strove in the way of Allah, and that you worshipped Allah until certainty came to you, and you fulfilled what was due upon you.
